messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] models not compiling with rcpp 0.11.0
parts:
On Mon, Feb 3, 2014 at 5:27 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Is there some way we can insulate ourselves from Rcpp
changing out from under us?

We could rewrite RStan as an R extension without Rcpp, we'd just have to create an API/adapter (dongle?) to bridge the gap that Rcpp fills currently.  Not a hard task, but a tedious one.  See: http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#System-and-foreign-language-interfaces

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] models not compiling with rcpp 0.11.0
parts:
I was thinking more along the lines of fixing a version of Rcpp!

Is the reason this is a problem that people will update Rcpp and
then we automatically use the latest.

I hate these kind of automatically filling-in dependencies. I'd
rather be able to update on our own schedule.

- Bob

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] models not compiling with rcpp 0.11.0
parts: Unlike Python's virtualenv, I didn't think we could enforce a version of Rcpp without breaking the user's ability to use another version elsewhere in the "global" or "user" install locations...?  What happens when one package wants XYZ 1.0 and another wants XYZ 1.1?  Maybe this is my limited knowledge of R showing.  Reading more about it shows that you can use "Imports" instead of "Depends" to achieve this, and it's possible to have R install the dependency in a package-specific location/path rather than the global/user path.
